Can we get information on "why"?  

Do we need to write extra code like we do for avahi, etc. in order to make this useful?

Do we need to disable the version advertisement?  That seems like a potential security concern.

it will be used for network discovery and network troubleshooting.

need to implement D-bus configuration to enable/disable lldp, so that this feature can be enabled when needed, I don't see any other extra code changes needed.

firmware version advertisement in local network is security concern??

> firmware version advertisement in local network is security concern??

Potentially.  We should see what bmcweb does by default and do that here too, right?

By advertising your version publicly, without authentication, you are potentially advertising known vulnerabilities.
got it, then I will check and turn off advertising firmware version

lldpd has given options to disable publishing firmware versions and override description required. 

Here is details of interface with lldpd publish

Interface:    eth0
  Administrative status: RX and TX
  Chassis:     
    ChassisID:    mac 07:94:ff:61:ef:84
    SysName:      p10bmc
    SysDescr:     eBMC
    MgmtIP:       9.x.x.177
    MgmtIface:    2
    MgmtIP:       2002:903:15f:325:a94:efff:fe81:ff84
    MgmtIface:    2
    Capability:   Bridge, off
    Capability:   Router, off
    Capability:   Wlan, off
    Capability:   Station, on
  Port:        
    PortID:       mac 07:84:ff:71:af:84
    PortDescr:    eth0
  TTL:          120
Done

Too bad recipe doesn't have a PACKAGECONFIG for this.  Also, I see over in https://grok.openbmc.org/xref/openbmc/openbmc/meta-openembedded/meta-networking/recipes-daemons/lldpd/lldpd_1.0.18.bb?r=73bd93f1#25 that the base recipe passes in a couple of "--with-privsep". Are you sure the compile handles both enables and disables of it correctly?

Actually "--with-privsep" needs new lldpd user to support privilege separation and lldpd fails to start without lldpd user and we don't need privilege separation
yes with this commit i see privilege separation disabled and lldpd started with existing root user on bmc
Doesn't the recipe create these users by default?  Why aren't we allowing that to work as already defined?
no recipe does not create lldpd user, I see service fails for lldpd user

Pretty sure it does:

https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/e81f073e0441dfd5b70f93b46d13470bb13fa12f/meta-openembedded/meta-networking/recipes-daemons/lldpd/lldpd_1.0.18.bb#L20

We need to investigate why this isn't working rather than disabling that functionality.
Its not creating lldpd user by default, it works if we create lldpd user before starting lldpd service

I am debugging why its not created user default and I don't any benefit of enabling this feature.

If were are having this new user then we need to also think about how this new lldpd user handled and impact other use-cases
I think we can go ahead with this change, since its functionally working same with this option disabled
I don't see any benefit of enabling this feature.

With this recipe lldpd user gets  created in rootfs but after flashing image to BMC there I don't see lldpd user on BMC, could not figure out reason yet.

this option does not have impact on lldp functionality, I can enable this option later after I figure out this issue. can we proceed with this is base commit.

"I couldn't figure this out" doesn't inspire confidence for merging a commit. ;)

At a minimum, please leave a comment in the recipe as to why this is there.

When any new daemon creates new user, it's not reflecting in next immediate code update unless there is factory reset involved.
looks like we need to put additional logic in openbmc to handle create user across code updates
Done
Where does this information come from on the BMC?  What is the "identity", what are "capabilities" in this context?
system name, ethernet port number, management address and Mac address.

Yes, please enumerate what we are planning to support so that people are not caught off guard by you publishing information on their system they weren't expecting.

Again, where does this come from?

Plan to disable lldp by default, only when Admin Enables LLDP then lldpd going to publish these details.

lldpd queries the system for available interfaces (e.g., /sys/class/net/ on Linux).
It retrieves information like MAC addresses and interface details and uses gethostname to get system name.

LLDP used for discovering network devices at the Data Link Layer, Works with Ethernet. there is Port schema which talks about LLDP

yes networks is going to control lldp enable/disable on each ethernet interface
